I joined a gym near my house last month.
I had never really exercised before, so I felt nervous about it.
My friend told me it would be easy to start.
On my first day, I walked in and looked around slowly.
There were many machines, and I didn't know how to use any of them.
Everyone else seemed to know exactly what to do already.
I found a treadmill and decided to start there.
I pressed a few buttons and started walking slowly at first.
After a few minutes, I felt more comfortable and walked a little faster.
Then I tried to run for a short time.
My legs felt fine at first, but I got tired much faster than I expected.
I had to stop and walk again after only two minutes.
I looked at the people running next to me on other treadmills.
They didn't look tired at all, even after a long time.
I wondered how long they had been coming to this gym.
After the treadmill, I tried a few weight machines nearby.
I picked the lightest weight I could find on each one.
Even that felt harder than I imagined it would be.
A trainer walked by and noticed me struggling with one machine.
He stopped and showed me the correct way to sit and pull the handle.
My old way was actually completely wrong the whole time, which explained why it felt so hard.
He was kind and patient, and he answered a few more of my questions.
He told me that everyone feels lost on their very first day.
He said it gets easier after just a few visits, and he was right about that.
I left the gym feeling tired but also proud of myself.
My legs were sore, and my arms felt weak and shaky.
Still, I had done something completely new, and that felt good, even if my body disagreed a little.
The next morning, I could barely walk down the stairs at home.
My whole body hurt in places I didn't even know could hurt.
I laughed at myself a little about it, holding the wall for balance.
I went back to the gym three days later, once the soreness slowly faded.
This time, I felt slightly less lost than before.
I even remembered how to use the treadmill without checking the buttons twice.
Now, I go three times a week, and it finally feels normal.
